name: Math Lessons for a Living Education
line: A parent teaches Math Lessons for a Living Education from a storybook. AMP places, checks and reviews on its own.
description: AMP vs Math Lessons for a Living Education: a story-led book a parent teaches for grades 1 to 6, or practice that places, checks and reviews itself.
verdict: Math Lessons for a Living Education is a gentle, story-led course for grades 1 to 6, taught by a parent from a full-color workbook, for $39.19 a level at the publisher's sale price [1][2]. AMP costs more. It does the work a book leaves to the adult: it finds the level in each part of math, checks and explains every answer as it is given, and brings each skill back on a schedule set for the learner.

reasons.title: Mistakes are explained while the problem is still there
reasons.body: Math Lessons for a Living Education is a printed workbook, so the adult checks a lesson's work after it is done [1]. AMP marks each answer the moment it is given and shows the correct answer and the worked steps before the next problem. The learner sees why at once, and no one has a page to grade.

reasons.title: A level for each part of math, not one book
reasons.body: The series places a child with a free Readiness Test for each level, then follows that level's lessons in order [1][5]. AMP keeps a separate level in each of 14 strands and finds them inside the first 24 problems, with no test for the adult to give or score. A child who is quick with shapes and unsure with fractions gets work at both heights in the same session.

reasons.title: A gap is traced back to where it starts
reasons.body: We found no mastery rule on the series' product pages; the adult judges when a child is ready to move on [1][3][4]. In AMP a skill is Strong at four of the last five answers right without help, and an answer after a hint does not count. Two misses in a row send practice back to what the skill builds on, so a gap is fixed where it starts.

reasons.title: Review timed to the learner, not to the page
reasons.body: The books build review in, with optional review activities, and Level 5 opens and closes with six review lessons [3][4]. That review falls at the same page for every child. AMP brings each learned skill back after 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and a month, mixed with other topics, and a miss starts the schedule over.

reasons.title: The adult's time goes to the child, not the answer key
reasons.body: Math Lessons for a Living Education is built for a parent who teaches: a daily schedule, a lesson to read together, and a Teaching Companion with guidance on manipulatives and learning styles [1][6]. In AMP the adult has nothing to plan, teach or grade. An adult who wants to teach finds a parent guide in each of 961 reference lessons, and every printed workbook comes with a key that shows the worked steps.

reasons.title: From counting to precalculus, and paper made for each child
reasons.body: The series runs from grade 1 to grade 6, and every child works in the same printed book [1][5]. AMP runs from counting through precalculus in one program. It prints unlimited workbooks built from each learner's own record, with worked answer keys, and results entered from paper count toward the learner's level.

rows.price: $39.19 per paperback level; Levels 1 to 5 list at $48.99. eBook $34.29. Level 6 teacher's guide sold separately [1][2][5]. One-time purchase.
rows.buyers: Anyone, as printed books or eBooks from the publisher's online store [1]. No subscription.
rows.range: Levels 1 to 6 for grades 1 to 6 [1][5]. Principles of Mathematics, a separate series, covers grades 7 and 8 [7].
rows.start: A free Readiness Test PDF for each level. The adult reads the result and picks the book [1][5].
rows.teaching: A parent teaches from the book: short stories, copywork, oral narration and hands-on manipulatives [1][3][6]. Optional video lessons sold separately [9].
rows.next: The next lesson in the book: 36 lessons a level on a daily schedule, in a fixed order [1][3].
rows.mastery: No mastery rule found on its product pages. The adult decides when to move on [1][3][4].
rows.review: Optional review activities, and at Level 5 six review lessons at each end [3][4]. The same for every child.
rows.print: Full-color, perforated, three-hole-punched workbooks of 344 to 396 pages [1][3][5]. One book for every child at that level.
rows.adult: Reads and teaches each lesson, sets out manipulatives, checks the work and sets the pace, following a daily schedule [1][6].
rows.reports: None built in; the adult keeps records. The Level 6 teacher's guide includes quizzes [5]. Principles of Mathematics has a downloadable assessment review test [7].
rows.evidence: None cited on its product pages. No entry in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report as of November 2026 [11][12].

theirs: Math Lessons for a Living Education is a math series from Master Books, a Christian homeschool imprint of New Leaf Publishing Group in Green Forest, Arkansas [1][10]. Angela O'Dell wrote it [1]. Levels 1 to 6 cover grades 1 to 6 [1][5]. For grades 7 and 8 the publisher sells Principles of Mathematics, by a different author, and it also sells algebra and consumer math books [2][7]. A Christian worldview is a stated aim of the books [6][7].

Each level is a full-color workbook, and Levels 1 to 5 each hold 36 lessons laid out on a daily schedule [1][3]. Lessons take 15 to 30 minutes in the early levels and about 30 at Level 6 [1][3][4][5]. A lesson weaves together a short story, copywork, oral narration and a hands-on activity; at Level 1 the story follows twins named Charlie and Charlotte [1]. Every level has a section of manipulatives to cut out, such as place value mats and charts [1][5].

The parent reads the lesson with the child, guides the activity and checks the work [1][6]. A separate Teaching Companion adds advice on manipulatives, ideas for different learning styles and math games [6]. Optional video lessons are sold through Master Books Academy and stream for 18 months from purchase [9].
credit: A low, one-time price: $39.19 for a paperback level at the sale price shown, with no subscription [1][2]. AMP costs far more.
Hands-on learning AMP does not offer: physical manipulatives, copywork, oral narration and a story running through the lessons [1][3][6].
Screen-free by design. A child works in a printed book, offline [1]. AMP prints workbooks, but its practice runs on a screen.
A Christian worldview built into the books [6][7]. AMP is math only.
Families rate it highly on the publisher's site: 4.9 of 5 from 893 reviews for Level 1 when we checked [1].

theirs: Its product pages cite no study of how much children learn with Math Lessons for a Living Education. The series has no entry in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report as of November 2026 [1][11][12].
What its pages do show is customer ratings, such as 4.9 of 5 from 893 reviews for Level 1 [1]. Ratings say how families feel about a book. They do not measure what children learned.
ours: Two of AMP's rules rest on findings that have held up. Mixed, spaced practice scored 62% against 38% for practice in blocks on the researchers' own test a month later, in a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations [13]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains averaged an effect of 0.49, against 0.05 for marking right or wrong only, across mixed ages and subjects, with smaller effects in primary and high school settings [14]. A well-made book can teach well and still leave both to the adult's calendar. AMP builds both into its rules, and we expect that to show in outcomes. That is our bet.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each is registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: You want screen-free math your child does in a book, with stories, copywork and hands-on manipulatives.
You want a Christian worldview woven into math lessons.
You enjoy teaching math yourself, a short lesson a day, from a schedule laid out for you.
You want to pay about $39 a level, once, with no subscription.
amp: You want every answer checked and explained the moment it is given, with nothing for you to grade.
Your child is ahead in one part of math and behind in another.
You want old skills to come back on a schedule set for your child, without planning it.
Your child is past grade 6, or you want one program through precalculus.
You love your book and want AMP beside it for practice and review.

questions.question: Is AMP more expensive than Math Lessons for a Living Education?
questions.answer: Yes. A paperback level costs $39.19 at the publisher's sale price, paid once [1]. AMP is $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child. For that it places the learner, chooses and checks every problem, schedules review, prints workbooks with worked keys, and runs from counting through precalculus.

questions.question: Can we use AMP alongside Math Lessons for a Living Education?
questions.answer: Yes. Many families can keep the book for its stories and hands-on lessons and use AMP for practice and review. AMP finds the learner's level on its own within the first 24 problems.

questions.question: Has Math Lessons for a Living Education been studied?
questions.answer: Its product pages cite no outcome study, and the series has no entry in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report as of November 2026 [1][11][12].

questions.question: Does AMP include Christian content?
questions.answer: No. AMP is math only. Families who want faith woven into lessons can keep a Christian curriculum and add AMP for practice.

questions.question: What happens if it isn't a fit?
questions.answer: AMP refunds personal payments in full within 30 days, no reason needed. Master Books takes back new, unused books within 30 days with a 15% restocking fee, and digital products are not refundable [8].
